q1_issues.issue: (Manner sk_predict_1 initially) mis-slots a temporal/sequence adverb into Manner, which is defined for adverbs answering 'how'.
(Member sk_sales_1 sale) types the plural 'sales' as a single sale; a plural carrying an aggregate measure takes GroupOf (cf. the crates example under Measures).

q2_gaps: a large-number scale word inside a money amount ('$6.9 billion') — no licensed magnitude multiplier exists, so the parse coins a billion_dollar unit that will not compare with plain dollar measures

a non-factive prediction whose content is carried by an NP complement ('predicted sales of between $6.9 billion and $7.5 billion') — sealing is finite-clause-only, so the predicted range ends up asserted as top-level fact rather than as the content of the prediction
a temporal adjunct whose object is a period NP ('at the end of the second quarter') — the Time role is defined for structured calendar terms and deictic/named constants, not for a minted witness

an ordinal naming a calendar/fiscal sub-period ('the second quarter') — Ordinal's scale slot is defined as the associated event or an explicit -est dimension, so a cycle like year has no licensed standing there
a two-sided numeric range ('between X and Y') has no named form; the parse composes MeasureAtLeast + MeasureAtMost
notes: The MeasureAtLeast/MeasureAtMost pair is a reasonable composition for the range, and 'end of the quarter' correctly takes the relational-noun PartOf rather than a coined head. The scale symbol price for a revenue figure is a stretch but is the closest dimension noun the Measures section offers.
